subject: Numeracy
title: Joining groups
objectives: Children will join two small groups and count all.
Children will tell a simple joining story.
content: Putting two groups together, counting all, and joining stories.
teachingActivities: Use real objects and stories first; model "two and three make five" in words; let children push two groups together and count all; do not introduce the plus sign until children are secure with the idea; keep totals to 5 at first and to 10 for confident children.
learnerActivities: Join two small groups and count all, and tell a simple joining story.
assessment: Observe whether each child joins two groups and counts all correctly to 5.
expectedOutcomes: Joins two groups and counts all to 5.
Tells a joining story with objects.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: working with a partner

lessons.title: Putting groups together
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will put two small groups together and count all.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make five in different ways, count beyond ten and find one more.
lessons.starter: Show two on one plate and one on another and say "Let us put them together and count all."
teacherActivities: Push two counters and one counter together and count all.
Give each child two small groups to join.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Push two counters and one counter together and count all. Children: Children count all the counters.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Two and one make three." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child two small groups to join. Children: Child joins and counts all.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many altogether?" Children: Child says the number.

practical.title: Join and count
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Join groups of one and two and count together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to join groups to make eight.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say altogether.
lessons.homeConnection: Join two small groups of fruit and count all.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put two small groups together and count all" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting all
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count all the objects after two groups have been joined.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make five in different ways, count beyond ten and find one more.
lessons.starter: Put two cows and three sheep in a field and say "How many animals altogether?"
teacherActivities: Show two groups of animals and count each group.
Put the groups together and count all.
Say "Two and three make five altogether."
Let children make their own groups to join.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two groups of animals and count each group. Children: Children count each group.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the groups together and count all. Children: Children count all the animals.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Two and three make five altogether." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children make their own groups to join. Children: Child joins and counts.

practical.title: Farm joining
steps: Join the groups in a field.
practical.safety: Use large toy animals and supervise closely so animals are not thrown. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Join groups of one and one then one and two.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three groups to join.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the animals away and say altogether.
lessons.homeConnection: Join groups of toys and count all.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count all the objects after two groups have been joined" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Joining stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will act out and tell short joining stories.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make five in different ways, count beyond ten and find one more.
lessons.starter: Tell a story: "Two children are at the gate. Two more come. How many children now?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with toys or children.
Tell a new story and let children act it.
Let a child tell a story for a friend to solve.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with toys or children. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many now?" Children: Child says the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Tell a new story and let children act it. Children: Child acts out the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child tell a story for a friend to solve. Children: Child tells a story.

practical.title: Story acting
practical.safety: Use large safe objects and keep children seated on chairs for bus stories. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Act the story with one to three objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a story with totals to ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Did we join or take away?

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the props and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a story about adding at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out and tell short joining stories" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making our own stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make up their own joining stories with toys.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make five in different ways, count beyond ten and find one more.
lessons.starter: Say "Today you are story makers. Choose some toys and tell a joining story."
teacherActivities: Show a story card and tell the story together.
Let each pair choose toys and make a story.
Let pairs tell their story to the class.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a story card and tell the story together. Children: Children listen and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each pair choose toys and make a story. Children: Pairs make a story.
Step 3. Teacher: Let pairs tell their story to the class. Children: Child tells the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask the class "How many altogether?" Children: Class says the number.

practical.title: Story makers
practical.safety: Use large toys only and supervise sharing. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Make a story together with one or two toys.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to write the story with a drawing.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the toys away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make up a joining story with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make up their own joining stories with toys" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 joining check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child joins groups and counts all.
successCriteria: Joins two groups and counts all
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can make five in different ways, count beyond ten and find one more.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: counters, farm and story.
At each station ask "How many altogether?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: counters, farm and story. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many altogether?" Children: Child joins and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Joining stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large objects. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use totals to three.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to join groups to make ten.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: joins two groups; counts all; acts a joining story; says the total.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child joins groups and counts all" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
